foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: The right lung is divided into three distinct lobes (superior, middle, and inferior) by the horizontal and oblique fissures, whereas the left lung has only two.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The presence of the liver causes which anatomical difference of the Kidneys and the Lungs?
choices: Left kidney slightly lower, Left lung slightly shorter
Left kidney slightly higher, Left lung slightly shorter
Right kidney lower, Right lung shorter
Right kidney higher, Right lung shorter
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Because the large liver occupies substantial space in the right upper abdominal quadrant, it pushes the right kidney lower down and compresses the diaphragm upward, making the right lung shorter.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Surfactant is produced by what cells in the alveoli?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Type II pneumocytes (alveolar cells) synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant, which decreases alveolar surface tension and prevents lung collapse.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The normal L:S Ratio to consider the newborn baby viable is
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A Lecithin-to-Sphingomyelin (L:S) ratio of 2:1 or greater in amniotic fluid signifies adequate fetal lung maturity and a low risk for Infant Respiratory Distress Syndrome.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Refers to the extra air that can be inhaled beyond the normal tidal volume
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) is defined as the maximum volume of air that can be forcefully inspired following a normal quiet tidal inhalation.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: This is the amount of air remained in the lungs after a forceful expiration
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Residual Volume (RV) is the amount of air that remains in the lungs even after a maximal, forced exhalation; it prevents complete alveolar collapse.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Casssandra, A 22 year old grade Agnostic, Asked you, how many spikes of bones are there in my ribs? Your best response is which of the following?
choices: We have 13 pairs of ribs Cassandra
We have 12 pairs of ribs Cassandra
Humans have 16 pairs of ribs, and that was noted by Vesalius in 1543
Humans have 8 pairs of ribs. 4 of which are floating
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Human skeletal anatomy typically consists of 12 pairs of ribs (24 total) attached posteriorly to the thoracic vertebrae.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is considered as the main muscle of respiration?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: The diaphragm is the primary muscle of inspiration, responsible for roughly 75% of the thoracic volume expansion during quiet breathing.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Cassandra asked you : How many air is there in the oxygen and how many does human requires?
choices: God is good, Man requires 21% of oxygen and we have 21% available in our air
Man requires 16% of oxygen and we have 35% available in our air
Man requires 10% of oxygen and we have 50% available in our air
Human requires 21% of oxygen and we have 21% available in our air
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Ambient air contains roughly 21% oxygen (FiO2 of 0.21), which is optimal to satisfy normal tissue metabolic requirements at standard atmospheric pressure.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is TRUE about Expiration?
choices: The length of which is half of the length of Inspiration
Stridor is commonly heard during expiration
Requires energy to be carried out
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Normal quiet expiration is a passive process resulting from the elastic recoil of the lungs and chest wall, requiring no active muscle contraction or energy expenditure.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is TRUE in postural drainage?
choices: Patient assumes position for 10 to 15 minutes
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Each position during postural drainage is typically maintained for 10 to 15 minutes to allow gravity sufficient time to drain secretions from targeted lung segments.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: All but one of the following is a purpose of steam inhalation
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Steam inhalation aims to dilate pathways, liquify mucus, and moisten dry membranes; promoting bronchoconstriction would narrow airways and worsen respiratory distress.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is NOT TRUE in steam inhalation?
choices: It is a dependent nursing action
Spout is put 12-18 inches away from the nose
Render steam inhalation for atleast 60 minutes
Cover the client’s eye with wash cloth to prevent irritation
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Steam inhalation therapy should typically last 10 to 15 minutes per session. Rendering it for 60 minutes or more can cause excessive heat exposure, airway irritation, or skin burns.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: When should a nurse suction a client?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Suctioning should strictly be performed PRN (as needed) when clinical indicators of airway secretions are present, rather than on a routine schedule, to prevent mucosal trauma and hypoxia.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Ernest Arnold Hamilton, a 60 year old American client was mobbed by teen gangsters near New york, Cubao. He was rushed to John John Hopio Medical Center and was Unconscious. You are his nurse and you are to suction his secretions. In which position should you place Mr. Hamilton?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: For an unconscious client, a side-lying (lateral) position prevents the tongue from obstructing the airway and allows secretions to drain out freely, reducing the risk of aspiration during suctioning.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: You are about to set the suction pressure to be used to Mr. Hamilton. You are using a Wall unit suction machine. How much pressure should you set the valve before suctioning Mr. Hamilton?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Standard wall suction pressure settings for adult clients typically range from 100 to 120 mmHg (or up to 150 mmHg depending on guidelines) to balance effective clearance and mucosal safety.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The wall unit is not functioning; You then try to use the portable suction equipment available. How much pressure of suction equipment is needed to prevent trauma to mucus membrane and air ways in case of portable suction units?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Portable suction unit gauges are calibrated differently in inches of mercury (inHg), where 10 to 15 inHg (commonly referenced in regional nursing exams alongside unit variations) represents safe adult operational limits.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: There are four catheter sizes available for use, which one of these should you use for Mr. Hamilton?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: For adult patients needing clearance of thicker secretions, standard suction catheter sizes typically range from 12 Fr to 18 Fr, with Fr. 18 being appropriate among the listed options.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following, if done by the nurse, indicates incompetence during suctioning an unconscious client?
choices: Measure the length of the suction catheter to be inserted by measuring from the tip of the nose, to the earlobe, to the xiphoid process
Use KY Jelly if suctioning nasopharyngeal secretion
The maximum time of suctioning should not exceed 15 seconds
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Measuring tip-of-nose to earlobe to xiphoid process (NEX) is used for sizing nasogastric (NG) tubes, not suction catheters. Suction catheter insertion depth should only be measured to the distance between tip of nose and earlobe (or insert until resistance/coughing is met).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is the initial sign of hypoxemia in an adult client?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Early compensatory clinical manifestations of hypoxemia include tachycardia (2) and restlessness/irritability (5) due to sympathetic nervous system stimulation.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which method of oxygenation least likely produces anxiety and apprehension?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A nasal cannula allows full movement of the mouth, easy speaking, and eating, minimizing claustrophobia and anxiety compared to tight-fitting face masks.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following oxygen delivery method can deliver 100% Oxygen at 15 LPM?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A Non-Rebreather mask equipped with a reservoir bag and one-way valves prevents rebreathing of room air, allowing delivery of high FiO2 concentrations approaching 90-100% at high flow rates (10-15 LPM).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is not true about OXYGEN?
choices: Oxygen is odorless, tasteless and colorless gas.
Excessive oxygen administration results in respiratory acidosis
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Excessive high-flow oxygen administration in COPD patients can induce respiratory depression and hypercapnia (retaining CO2), leading to respiratory acidosis, but oxygen gas itself does not inherently cause respiratory acidosis.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Roberto San Andres, A new nurse in the hospital is about to administer oxygen on patient with Respiratory distress. As his senior nurse, you should intervene if Roberto will:
choices: Uses venture mask in oxygen administration
Put a non rebreather mask in the patient before opening the oxygen source
Use a partial rebreather mask to deliver oxygen
Check for the doctor’s order for Oxygen administration
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Applying a mask before turning on the oxygen gas flow causes the patient to suffocate or rebreathe expired air trapped inside the mask, which can exacerbate hypoxia.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following will alert the nurse as an early sign of hypoxia?
choices: The client is coughing out blood
The client’s heart rate is 50 BPM
Client is frequently turning from side to side
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Restlessness, agitation, and frequent position changes (turning side to side) are classic initial signs of brain hypoxia driven by central nervous system irritation.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Miguelito de balboa, An OFW presents at the admission with an A:P Diameter ratio of 2:1, Which of the following associated finding should the nurse expect?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: An AP to transverse chest ratio of 2:1 (barrel chest) indicates chronic hyperinflation seen in severe COPD; chronic tissue hypoxia also produces digital clubbing of the fingers over time.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The best method of oxygen administration for client with COPD uses:
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Nasal cannula delivers low concentrations of oxygen (1-2 L/min) safely, maintaining oxygenation without blunting the hypoxic drive in chronic CO2 retainers.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Mang dagul, a 50 year old chronic smoker was brought to the E.R because of difficulty in breathing. Pleural effusion was the diagnosis and CTT was ordered. What does C.T.T Stands for?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: In clinical practice, CTT stands for Closed Tube Thoracotomy (or tube thoracostomy), referring to the insertion of a chest tube connected to a closed drainage unit.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Where will the CTT be inserted if we are to drain fluids accumulated in Mang dagul’s pleura?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Fluid accumulates in lower dependent areas due to gravity, requiring insertion into lower intercostal spaces such as the 8th or 9th ICS along the posterior/mid-axillary line.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: There is a continuous bubbling in the water sealed drainage system with suction. And oscillation is observed. As a nurse, what should you do?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Continuous gentle bubbling in the suction control chamber combined with tidal oscillation (tidaling) in the water-seal chamber indicates that the suction system is functioning normally.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is true about nutrition?
choices: It is the process in which food are broken down, for the body to use in growth and development
It is a process in which digested proteins, fats, minerals, vitamins and carbohydrates are transported into the circulation
It is a chemical process that occurs in the cell that allows for energy production, energy use, growth and tissue repair
It is the study of nutrients and the process in which they are use by the body
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Nutrition is defined broad-scope as the science and study of nutrients and food substances, including their ingestion, digestion, absorption, and metabolic utilization by the organism.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The majority of the digestion processes take place in the
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: The small intestine (specifically the duodenum and jejunum) receives digestive enzymes from the pancreas and liver, making it the primary site for chemical digestion and nutrient absorption.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: All of the following is true about digestion that occurs in the Mouth except
choices: It is where the digestion process starts
Mechanical digestion is brought about by mastication
The action of ptyalin or the salivary tyrpsin breaks down starches into maltose
Deglutition occurs after food is broken down into small pieces and well mixed with saliva
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Ptyalin is salivary amylase, not 'salivary trypsin'. Trypsin is a proteolytic enzyme produced exclusively by the pancreas.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following foods lowers the cardiac sphincter pressure?
choices: Roast beef, Steamed cauliflower and Rice
Orange juice, Non fat milk, Dry crackers
Decaffeinated coffee, Sky flakes crackers, Suman
Coffee with coffee mate, Bacon and Egg
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: High-fat foods (bacon, eggs) and caffeinated substances (coffee) significantly reduce Lower Esophageal Sphincter (LES / cardiac sphincter) tone, promoting gastroesophageal reflux.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Where does the digestion of carbohydrates start?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Carbohydrate breakdown begins immediately in the mouth through the mechanical action of chewing and the enzymatic action of salivary amylase (ptyalin).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Protein and Fat digestion begins where?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Protein digestion initiates in the stomach via pepsin activation by stomach acid, while gastric lipase also initiates minor preliminary breakdown of dietary fats.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: All but one is true about digestion that occurs in the Stomach
choices: Carbohydrates are the fastest to be digested, in about an hour
Fat is the slowest to be digested, in about 5 hours
HCl inhibits absorption of Calcium in the gastric mucosa
HCl converts pepsinogen to pepsin, which starts the complex process of protein digestion
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) actually enhances calcium absorption by maintaining an acidic pH that keeps calcium salts dissolved in an absorbable ionic state.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is NOT an enzyme secreted by the small intestine?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Amylase is produced and secreted by the salivary glands and the pancreas, not synthesized by the intestinal brush border.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The hormone secreted by the Small intestine that stimulates the production of pancreatic juice which primarily aids in buffering the acidic bolus passed by the Stomach
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Pancreozymin (closely related in function to secretin/CCK response pathways) stimulates the release of pancreatic enzymes and bicarbonate-rich digestive juices.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: When the duodenal enzyme sucrase acts on SUCROSE, which 2 monosaccharides are formed?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide composed of one glucose molecule and one fructose molecule linked together, which sucrase cleaves during hydrolysis.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: This is the enzyme secreted by the pancrease that completes the protein digestion
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Trypsin is a powerful pancreatic protease that hydrolyzes polypeptide chains into smaller peptides and amino acids within the small intestine.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The end product of protein digestion or the “Building blocks of Protein” is what we call
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Amino acids are the fundamental monomer subunits that link together via peptide bonds to form complex functional proteins.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Enzyme secreted by the small intestine after it detects a bolus of fatty food. This will contract the gallbladder to secrete bile and relax the sphincter of Oddi to aid in the emulsification of fats and its digestion.
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is released by duodenal cells in response to dietary fat and triggers gallbladder contraction and relaxation of the sphincter of Oddi.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is not true about the Large Intestine?
choices: It absorbs around 1 L of water making the feces around 75% water and 25% solid
The stool formed in the transverse colon is not yet well formed
It is a sterile body cavity
It is called large intestine because it is longer than the small intestine
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: The large intestine is not sterile; it hosts a dense and complex ecosystem of normal microbial flora (gut microbiome) necessary for fermentation and vitamin synthesis.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: This is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg water to 1 degree Celsius
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A kilocalorie (commonly referred to simply as a Calorie in dietary terms) is defined as the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kilogram of water by 1 degree Celsius.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Assuming a cup of rice provides 50 grams of carbohydrates. How many calories are there in that cup of rice?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Carbohydrates yield 4 calories per gram; multiplying 50 grams of carbohydrates by 4 kcal/g equals 200 calories.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: An average adult filipino requires how many calories in a day?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Standard dietary reference intakes set the average adult daily caloric requirement around 2,000 kcal/day to maintain basic metabolic and physical functions.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is true about an individual’s caloric needs?
choices: All individual have the same caloric needs
Females in general have higher BMR and therefore, require more calories
During cold weather, people need more calories due to increase BMR
Dinner should be the heaviest meal of the day
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Cold environments force the body to increase thermogenesis to maintain core temperature, which elevates the basal metabolic rate (BMR) and increases overall energy/caloric requirements.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Among the following people, who requires the greatest caloric intake?
choices: An individual in a long state of gluconeogenesis
An individual in a long state of glycogenolysis
An adolescent with a BMI of 25
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Gluconeogenesis is an energy-expensive metabolic state that breaks down non-carbohydrate substrates under severe metabolic stress or starvation, significantly heightening energy expenditure.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which nutrient deficiency is associated with the development of Pellagra, Dermatitis and Diarrhea?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Vitamin B3 (niacin) deficiency causes pellagra, classic for the '3 Ds': dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia (and eventually death if untreated).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which Vitamin is not given in conjunction with the intake of LEVODOPA in cases of Parkinson’s Disease due to the fact that levodopa increases its level in the body?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) acts as a cofactor for dopa decarboxylase, enhancing peripheral breakdown of levodopa before it can cross the blood-brain barrier and decreasing its therapeutic efficacy.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: A vitamin taken in conjunction with ISONIAZID to prevent peripheral neuritis
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Isoniazid (INH) competes with pyridoxal phosphate and increases Vitamin B6 excretion; supplementation with Pyridoxine (B6) prevents INH-induced peripheral neuropathy.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The inflammation of the Lips, Palate and Tongue is associated in the deficiency of this vitamin
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency leads to oral-ocular-genital syndromes, classically causing cheilosis (cracked lips), angular stomatitis, glossitis (inflamed tongue), and stomatitis.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Beri beri is caused by the deficiency of which Vitamin?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency results in beriberi, which manifests as dry beriberi (peripheral neuropathy) or wet beriberi (heart failure and edema).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is the best source of Vitamin E?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Plant-based vegetable oils (such as wheat germ, sunflower, and safflower oil) are among the richest dietary sources of alpha-tocopherol (Vitamin E).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Among the following foods, which food should you emphasize giving on an Alcoholic client?
choices: Pork liver and organ meats, Pork
Red meat, Eggs and Dairy products
Green leafy vegetables, Yellow vegetables, Cantaloupe and Dairy products
Chicken, Peanuts, Bananas, Wheat germs and yeasts
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Chronic alcohol use depletes thiamine (Vitamin B1) stores; pork, organ meats, and liver are rich in thiamine to prevent Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which food group should you emphasize giving on a pregnant mother in first trimester to prevent neural tube defects?
choices: Butter, Sardines, Tuna, Salmon, Egg yolk
Wheat germ, Vegetable Oil, soybeans, corn, peanuts
Organ meats, Green leafy vegetables, Liver, Eggs
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Organ meats, green leafy vegetables, liver, and eggs contain rich reserves of folate (Vitamin B9), which is essential during early organogenesis to prevent neural tube defects like spina bifida.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: A client taking Coumadin is to be educated on his diet. As a nurse, which of the following food should you instruct the client to avoid?
choices: Spinach, Green leafy vegetables, Cabbage, Liver
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Coumadin (warfarin) acts as a Vitamin K antagonist; consuming high amounts of Vitamin K-rich foods like spinach, cabbage, and liver antagonizes the anticoagulant effect.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Vitamin E plus this mineral works as one of the best anti oxidant in the body according to the latest research. They are combined with 5 Alpha reductase inhibitor to reduce the risk of acquiring prostate cancer
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Selenium functions synergistically with Vitamin E as an essential cofactor for glutathione peroxidase, protecting cellular membranes against oxidative damage.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Incident of prostate cancer is found to have been reduced on a population exposed in tolerable amount of sunlight. Which vitamin is associated with this phenomenon?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Sunlight exposure triggers cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) synthesis in the skin, which converted to its active form regulates cellular growth and exhibits protective antineoplastic properties.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Micronutrients are those nutrients needed by the body in a very minute amount. Which of the following vitamin is considered as a MICRONUTRIENT
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Iron is classified as a trace mineral (micronutrient) because body requirements are in trace amounts (milligrams), whereas calcium, phosphorus, and sodium are macrominerals.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Deficiency of this mineral results in tetany, osteomalacia, osteoporosis and rickets.
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Calcium is the primary structural mineral in bone tissue; its deficit impairs mineralization (causing rickets/osteomalacia) and increases neuromuscular excitability (leading to tetany).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Among the following foods, which has the highest amount of potassium per area of their meat?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Cantaloupe yields a remarkably high concentration of potassium relative to serving weight/volume, outperforming many other fresh fruits per unit.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: A client has HEMOSIDEROSIS. Which of the following drug would you expect to be given to the client?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Deferoxamine is an iron-chelating agent that binds free iron ions in plasma, facilitating excretion in cases of iron overload conditions like hemosiderosis or hemochromatosis.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following provides the richest source of Iron per area of their meat?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Organ meats, particularly pork liver, contain exceptionally dense concentrations of bioavailable heme iron compared to muscle meats or plant sources.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is considered the best indicator of nutritional status of an individual?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Weight reflects acute and recent alterations in nutritional status and fluid shifts, making it a sensitive baseline operational indicator in routine clinical assessments.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Jose Miguel, a 50 year old business man is 6’0 Tall and weights 179 lbs. As a nurse, you know that Jose Miguel is :
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A height of 6'0" (1.83 m) and weight of 179 lbs (81.2 kg) yields a BMI of approximately 24.3 kg/m², which falls within the standard normal range (18.5 - 24.9 kg/m²).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Jose Miguel is a little bit nauseous. Among the following beverages, Which could help relieve JM’s nausea?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Flat or carbonated cola drinks (like Coke) contain concentrated syrup mixtures and phosphoric acid that help soothe gastric smooth muscle spasms and relieve mild nausea.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is the first sign of dehydration?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Thirst is the primary defense mechanism triggered early by osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus in response to small increases in serum osmolality.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: What Specific gravity lab result is compatible with a dehydrated client?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Normal urine specific gravity ranges from 1.005 to 1.030; a highly elevated specific gravity like 1.039 reflects concentrated urine output typical of hemoconcentration and dehydration.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which hematocrit value is expected in a dehydrated male client?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Fluid volume deficit leads to severe hemoconcentration, resulting in artificially elevated hematocrit levels well above the normal adult male range of 40-54% (e.g., 67%).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following statement by a client with prolonged vomiting indicates the initial onset of hypokalemia?
choices: I felt my heart beat just right now
Nurse, help! My legs are cramping
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Hypokalemia alters resting membrane potential, classically presenting first with neuromuscular excitability changes like muscle weakness, pain, and calf/leg cramps.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is not an anti-emetic?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Alevaire (tyloxapol) is a detergent/mucolytic aerosol used historically to liquefy pulmonary secretions, whereas the others possess antiemetic or anticholinergic actions.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which is not a clear liquid diet?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A clear liquid diet consists of fluids that are transparent at room temperature; adding creamer (Coffee-mate) turns coffee opaque, placing it into the full liquid category.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is included in a full liquid diet?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Popsicles melt into smooth liquid at body temperature without solid residue, making them appropriate for a full liquid (and clear liquid) dietary regimen.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which food is included in a BLAND DIET?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Creamed potatoes are smooth, non-irritating, low-fiber, and non-spicy, making them ideal for gastric mucosa protection on a bland diet.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following if done by the nurse, is correct during NGT Insertion?
choices: Measure the amount of the tube to be inserted from the Tip of the nose, to the earlobe, to the xiphoid process
Soak the NGT in a basin of ice water to facilitate easy insertion
Check the placement of the tube by introducing 10 cc of sterile water and auscultating for bubbling sound
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: The correct physical measurement for proper nasogastric tube insertion length is from the tip of the nose to the earlobe, and then down to the xiphoid process (NEX measurement).

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is the BEST method in assessing for the correct placement of the NGT?
choices: Immerse tip of the tube in water to check for bubbles produced
Aspirating gastric content to check if the content is acidic
Instilling air in the NGT and listening for a gurgling sound at the epigastric area
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Radiographic verification (X-ray) remains the absolute gold standard to confirm anatomical placement of a newly inserted NGT prior to initiating enteral feedings or medications.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: A terminally ill cancer patient is scheduled for an NGT feeding today. How should you position the patient?
choices: Bring the client into a chair
Slightly elevated right side lying position
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Assisting the client to sit upright in a chair utilizes gravity optimal for stomach emptying and minimizes aspiration risk compared to bed positioning whenever tolerated.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: A client is scheduled for NGT Feeding. Checking the residual volume, you determined that he has 40 cc residual from the last feeding. You reinstill the 40 cc of residual volume and added the 250 cc of feeding ordered by the doctor. You then instill 60 cc of water to clear the lumen and the tube. How much will you put in the client’s chart as input?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Total new fluid input consists of the formula (250 cc) plus the water flush (60 cc), equaling 310 cc. Re-instilled gastric residual (40 cc) was already inside the stomach, so it is not calculated as new fluid intake.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following if done by a nurse indicates deviation from the standards of NGT feeding?
choices: Do not give the feeding and notify the doctor of residual of the last feeding is greater than or equal to 50 ml
Height of the feeding should be 12 inches about the tube point of insertion to allow slow introduction of feeding
Ask the client to position in supine position immediately after feeding to prevent dumping syndrome
Clamp the NGT before all of the water is instilled to prevent air entry in the stomach
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Placing a patient flat on their back (supine) immediately after tube feeding drastically elevates aspiration risk; patients should remain elevated in High or Semi-Fowler's position for at least 30-60 minutes.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: What is the most common problem in TUBE FEEDING?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Diarrhea is the most frequent gastrointestinal complication associated with enteral tube feedings, often caused by hyperosmolar formulas, rapid infusion rates, or bacterial contamination.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is TRUE in colostomy feeding?
choices: Hold the syringe 18 inches above the stoma and administer the feeding slowly
Pour 30 ml of water before and after feeding administration
Insert the ostomy feeding tube 1 inch towards the stoma
A Pink stoma means that circulation towards the stoma is all well
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Flushing 30 mL of water before and after enteral administration ensures tube patency, clears remaining formula from the lumen, and maintains proper hydration balance.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: A client with TPN suddenly develops tremors, dizziness, weakness and diaphoresis. The client said “I feel weak” You saw that his TPN is already empty and another TPN is scheduled to replace the previous one but its provision is already 3 hours late. Which of the following is the probable complication being experienced by the client?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Abruptly stopping concentrated dextrose infusion in TPN leads to rebound hypoglycemia because hyperinsulinemia remains elevated after the glucose intake stops.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: To assess the adequacy of food intake, which of the following assessment parameters is best used?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: A 3-day diet recall provides a representative, structured quantitative sample of actual nutrient and caloric intake over time compared to a single 24-hour window.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The vomiting center is found in the
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: The emetic center (vomiting center) and chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) are located in the medulla oblongata within the brainstem.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The most threatening complication of vomiting in client’s with stroke is
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Stroke clients often suffer from impaired airway reflexes and dysphagia; vomiting poses a direct, immediate threat of aspiration pneumonia or airway obstruction.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which among this food is the richest source of Iron?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Legumes such as mongo (mung beans) supply higher concentrated non-heme iron content per serving weight relative to standard green leafy vegetables.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which of the following is a good source of Vitamin A?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Animal liver serves as the organ storing preformed Vitamin A (retinoids), providing one of the highest concentrated dietary sources available.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The most important nursing action before gastrostomy feeding is
choices: Assess for patency of the tube
Check the placement of the tube
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Confirming patency ensures the tube is free from blockages or kinks before introducing liquid formula, preventing complications such as tube displacement or regurgitation.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The primary advantage of gastrostomy feeding is
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Because a gastrostomy tube inserts directly through the abdominal wall into the stomach, it bypasses the esophagus completely and leaves the lower esophageal sphincter intact.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: What is the BMI Of Budek, weighing 120 lbs and has a height of 5 feet 7 inches.
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Converting 120 lbs to kg (~54.4 kg) and 5'7" to meters (~1.70 m): BMI = 54.4 / (1.70)² ≈ 18.8, which rounds to approximately 19.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: Which finding is consistent with PERNICIOUS ANEMIA?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency (pernicious anemia) causes glossitis characterized by a smooth, beefy red, tender tongue.

foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.question: The nurse is browsing the chart of the patient and notes a normal serum lipase level. Which of the following is a normal serum lipase value?
foundation-oxygenation-nutrition.explanation: Standard reference ranges for serum lipase generally extend up to 160-200 U/L depending on lab testing assays, making 200 U/L the closest target standard.

foundation-exam-1.question: Jake is complaining of shortness of breath. The nurse assesses his respiratory rate to be 30 breaths per minute and documents that Jake is tachypneic. The nurse understands that tachypnea means:
choices: Pulse rate greater than 100 beats per minute
Respiratory rate greater than 20 breaths per minute
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Respiratory rate greater than 20 breaths per minute. A respiratory rate of greater than 20 breaths per minute is tachypnea. A blood pressure of 140/90 is considered hypertension. Pulse greater than 100 beats per minute is tachycardia. Frequent bowel sounds refer to hyper-active bowel sounds.

foundation-exam-1.question: The nurse listens to Mrs. Sullen’s lungs and notes a hissing sound or musical sound. The nurse documents this as:
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (A) Wheezes. Wheezes are indicated by continuous, lengthy, musical; heard during inspiration or expiration. Rhonchi are usually coarse breath sounds. Gurgles are loud gurgling, bubbling sound. Vesicular breath sounds are low pitch, soft intensity on expiration.

foundation-exam-1.question: The nurse in charge measures a patient’s temperature at 101 degrees F. What is the equivalent centigrade temperature?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (B) 37.95 degrees C. To convert °F to °C use this formula, ( °F – 32 ) (0.55). While when converting °C to °F use this formula, ( °C x 1.8) + 32. Note that 0.55 is 5/9 and 1.8 is 9/5.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which approach to problem solving tests any number of solutions until one is found that works for that particular problem?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (D) Trial and error. The trial and error method of problem solving isn’t systematic (as in the scientific method of problem solving) routine, or based on inner prompting (as in the intuitive method of problem solving).

foundation-exam-1.question: What is the order of the nursing process?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Assessing, diagnosing, planning, implementing, evaluating. The correct order of the nursing process is assessing, diagnosing, planning, implementing, evaluating.

foundation-exam-1.question: During the planning phase of the nursing process, which of the following is the outcome?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Nursing care plan. The outcome, or the product of the planning phase of the nursing process is a Nursing care plan.

foundation-exam-1.question: What is an example of a subjective data?
choices: Heart rate of 68 beats per minute
Client verbalized, “I feel pain when urinating.”
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Client verbalized, “I feel pain when urinating.”. Subjective data are those that can be described only by the person experiencing it. Therefore, only the patient can describe or verify whether he is experiencing pain or not.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which expected outcome is correctly written?
choices: “The patient will feel less nauseated in 24 hours.”
“The patient will eat the right amount of food daily.”
“The patient will identify all the high-salt food from a prepared list by discharge.”
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) “The patient will identify all the high-salt food from a prepared list by discharge.”. Expected outcomes are specific, measurable, realistic statements of goal attainment. The phrases “right amount”, “less nauseated” and “enough sleep” are vague and not measurable.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which of the following behaviors by Nurse Jane Robles demonstrates that she understands well th elements of effecting charting?
choices: She writes in the chart using a no. 2 pencil.
She noted: appetite is good this afternoon.
She signs on the medication sheet after administering the medication.
She signs her charting as follow: J.R
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) She signs on the medication sheet after administering the medication. A nurse should record a nursing intervention (ex. Giving medications) after performing the nursing intervention (not before). Recording should also be done using a pen, be complete, and signed with the nurse’s full name and title.

foundation-exam-1.question: What is the disadvantage of computerized documentation of the nursing process?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Concern for privacy. A patient’s privacy may be violated if security measures aren’t used properly or if policies and procedures aren’t in place that determines what type of information can be retrieved, by whom, and for what purpose.

foundation-exam-1.question: The theorist who believes that adaptation and manipulation of stressors are related to foster change is:
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (B) Sister Callista Roy. Sister Roy’s theory is called the adaptation theory and she viewed each person as a unified biophysical system in constant interaction with a changing environment. Orem’s theory is called self-care deficit theory and is based on the belief that individual has a need for self-care actions. King’s theory is the Goal attainment theory and described nursing as a helping profession that assists individuals and groups in society to attain, maintain, and restore health. Henderson introduced the nature of nursing model and identified the 14 basic needs.

foundation-exam-1.question: Formulating a nursing diagnosis is a joint function of:
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (B) Nurse and patient. Although diagnosing is basically the nurse’s responsibility, input from the patient is essential to formulate the correct nursing diagnosis.

foundation-exam-1.question: Mrs. Caperlac has been diagnosed to have hypertension since 10 years ago. Since then, she had maintained low sodium, low fat diet, to control her blood pressure. This practice is viewed as:
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Health belief. Health belief of an individual influences his/her preventive health behavior.

foundation-exam-1.question: Becky is on NPO since midnight as preparation for blood test. Adreno-cortical response is activated. Which of the following is an expected response?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (D) Decreased urine output. Adreno-cortical response involves release of aldosterone that leads to retention of sodium and water. This results to decreased urine output.

foundation-exam-1.question: What nursing action is appropriate when obtaining a sterile urine specimen from an indwelling catheter to prevent infection?
choices: Use sterile gloves when obtaining urine.
Open the drainage bag and pour out the urine.
Disconnect the catheter from the tubing and get urine.
Aspirate urine from the tubing port using a sterile syringe.
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (D) Aspirate urine from the tubing port using a sterile syringe. The nurse should aspirate the urine from the port using a sterile syringe to obtain a urine specimen. Opening a closed drainage system increase the risk of urinary tract infection.

foundation-exam-1.question: A client is receiving 115 ml/hr of continuous IVF. The nurse notices that the venipuncture site is red and swollen. Which of the following interventions would the nurse perform first?
choices: Place a clod towel on the site
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (A) Stop the infusion. The sign and symptoms indicate extravasation so the IVF should be stopped immediately and put warm not cold towel on the affected site.

foundation-exam-1.question: The nurse enters the room to give a prescribed medication but the patient is inside the bathroom. What should the nurse do?
choices: Leave the medication at the bedside and leave the room.
After few minutes, return to that patient’s room and do not leave until the patient takes the medication.
Instruct the patient to take the medication and leave it at the bedside.
Wait for the patient to return to bed and just leave the medication at the bedside.
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (B) After few minutes, return to that patient’s room and do not leave until the patient takes the medication. This is to verify or to make sure that the medication was taken by the patient as directed.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which of the following is inappropriate nursing action when administering NGT feeding?
choices: Place the feeding 20 inches above the pint if insertion of NGT.
Instill 60ml of water into the NGT after feeding.
Assist the patient in fowler’s position.
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (A) Place the feeding 20 inches above the pint if insertion of NGT. The height of the feeding is above 12 inches above the point of insertion, bot 20 inches. If the height of feeding is too high, this results to very rapid introduction of feeding. This may trigger nausea and vomiting.

foundation-exam-1.question: A female patient is being discharged after thyroidectomy. After providing the medication teaching. The nurse asks the patient to repeat the instructions. The nurse is performing which professional role?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (D) Educator. When teaching a patient about medications before discharge, the nurse is acting as an educator. A caregiver provides direct care to the patient. The nurse acts as s patient advocate when making the patient’s wishes known to the doctor.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which data would be of greatest concern to the nurse when completing the nursing assessment of a 68-year-old woman hospitalized due to Pneumonia?
choices: Oriented to date, time and place
Capillary refill greater than 3 seconds and buccal cyanosis
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Capillary refill greater than 3 seconds and buccal cyanosis. Capillary refill greater than 3 seconds and buccal cyanosis indicate decreased oxygen to the tissues which requires immediate attention/intervention. Oriented to date, time and place, hemoglobin of 13 g/dl are normal data.

foundation-exam-1.question: During a change-of-shift report, it would be important for the nurse relinquishing responsibility for care of the patient to communicate. Which of the following facts to the nurse assuming responsibility for care of the patient?
choices: That the patient verbalized, “My headache is gone.”
That the patient’s barium enema performed 3 days ago was negative
Patient’s NGT was removed 2 hours ago
Patient’s family came for a visit this morning.
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Patient’s NGT was removed 2 hours ago. The change-of-shift report should indicate significant recent changes in the patient’s condition that the nurse assuming responsibility for care of the patient will need to monitor. The other options are not critical enough to include in the report.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which statement is the most appropriate goal for a nursing diagnosis of diarrhea?
choices: “The patient will experience decreased frequency of bowel elimination.”
“The patient will give a stool specimen for laboratory examinations.”
“The patient will save urine for inspection by the nurse.
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (A) “The patient will experience decreased frequency of bowel elimination.” The goal is the opposite, healthy response of the problem statement of the nursing diagnosis. In this situation, the problem statement is diarrhea.

foundation-exam-1.question: Which of the following is the most important purpose of planning care with this patient?
choices: Expansion of the current taxonomy of nursing diagnosis
Incorporation of both nursing and medical diagnoses in patient care
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (C) Making of individualized patient care. To be effective, the nursing care plan developed in the planning phase of the nursing process must reflect the individualized needs of the patient.

foundation-exam-1.question: Using Maslow’s hierarchy of basic human needs, which of the following nursing diagnoses has the highest priority?
choices: Ineffective breathing pattern related to pain, as evidenced by shortness of breath.
Anxiety related to impending surgery, as evidenced by insomnia.
Risk of injury related to autoimmune dysfunction
Impaired verbal communication related to tracheostomy, as evidenced by inability to speak.
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (A) Ineffective breathing pattern related to pain, as evidenced by shortness of breath. Physiologic needs (ex. Oxygen, fluids, nutrition) must be met before lower needs (such as safety and security, love and belongingness, self-esteem and self-actualization) can be met. Therefore, physiologic needs have the highest priority.

foundation-exam-1.question: When performing an abdominal examination, the patient should be in a supine position with the head of the bed at what position?
foundation-exam-1.explanation: (D) 0 degree. The patient should be positioned with the head of the bed completely flattened to perform an abdominal examination. If the head of the bed is elevated, the abdominal muscles and organs can be bunched up, altering the findings.

foundation-exam-2.question: A patient is wearing a soft wrist-safety device. Which of the following nursing assessment is considered abnormal?
choices: Bluish fingernails, cool and pale fingers
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (D) Bluish fingernails, cool and pale fingers. A safety device on the wrist may impair blood circulation. Therefore, the nurse should assess the patient for signs of impaired circulation such as bluish fingernails, cool and pale fingers. Palpable radial and ulnar pulses, capillary refill within 3 seconds are all normal findings.

foundation-exam-2.question: Pia’s serum sodium level is 150 mEq/L. Which of the following food items does the nurse instruct Pia to avoid?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Sardines. The normal serum sodium level is 135 to 145 mEq/L, the client is having hypernatremia. Pia should avoid food high in sodium like processed food. Broccoli, cabbage and tomatoes are good source of Vitamin C.

foundation-exam-2.question: Jason, 3 years old vomited. His mom stated, “He vomited 6 ounces of his formula this morning.” This statement is an example of:
choices: objective data from a secondary source
objective data from a primary source
subjective data from a primary source
subjective data from a secondary source
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (A) Objective data from a secondary source. Jason is the primary source; his mother is a secondary source. The data is objective because it can be perceived by the senses, verified by another person observing the same patient, and tested against accepted standards or norms.

foundation-exam-2.question: Which of the following is a nursing diagnosis?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (A) Hypethermia. Hyperthermia is a NANDA-approved nursing diagnosis. Diabetes Mellitus, Angina and Chronic Renal Failure are medical diagnoses.

foundation-exam-2.question: What is the characteristic of the nursing process?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (D) Goal-oriented. The nursing process is goal-oriented. It is also systematic, patient-centered, and dynamic.

foundation-exam-2.question: A skin lesion which is fluid-filled, less than 1 cm in size is called:
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Vesicle. Vesicle is a circumscribed circulation containing serous fluid or blood and less than 1 cm (ex. Blister, chicken pox).

foundation-exam-2.question: During application of medication into the ear, which of the following is inappropriate nursing action?
choices: In an adult, pull the pinna upward.
Instill the medication directly into the tympanic membrane.
Warm the medication at room or body temperature.
Press the tragus of the ear a few times to assist flow of medication into the ear canal.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Instill the medication directly into the tympanic membrane. During the application of medication it is inappropriate to instill the medication directly into the tympanic membrane. The right thing to do is instill the medication along the lateral wall of the auditory canal.

foundation-exam-2.question: Which of the following is appropriate nursing intervention for a client who is grieving over the death of her child?
choices: Tell her not to cry and it will be better.
Provide opportunity to the client to tell their story.
Encourage her to accept or to replace the lost person.
Discourage the client in expressing her emotions.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Provide opportunity to the client to tell their story. Providing a grieving person an opportunity to tell their story allows the person to express feelings. This is therapeutic in assisting the client resolve grief.

foundation-exam-2.question: It is the gradual decrease of the body’s temperature after death.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) Algor mortis. Algor mortis is the decrease of the body’s temperature after death. Livor mortis is the discoloration of the skin after death. Rigor mortis is the stiffening of the body that occurs about 2-4 hours after death.

foundation-exam-2.question: When performing an admission assessment on a newly admitted patient, the nurse percusses resonance. The nurse knows that resonance heard on percussion is most commonly heard over which organ?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (D) Lung. Resonance is loud, low-pitched and long duration that’s heard most commonly over an air-filled tissue such as a normal lung.

foundation-exam-2.question: The nurse is aware that Bell’s palsy affects which cranial nerve?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (D) 7th CN (Facial). Bell’s palsy is the paralysis of the motor component of the 7th cranial nerve, resulting in facial sag, inability to close the eyelid or the mouth, drooling, flat nasolabial fold and loss of taste on the affected side of the face.

foundation-exam-2.question: Prolonged deficiency of Vitamin B9 leads to:
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) Megaloblastic anemia. Prolonged Vitamin B9 deficiency will lead to megaloblastic anemia while pernicious anemia results in deficiency in Vitamin B12. Prolonged deficiency of Vitamin C leads to scurvy and Pellagra results in deficiency in Vitamin B3.

foundation-exam-2.question: Nurse Cherry is teaching a 72 year old patient about a newly prescribed medication. What could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about the newly prescribed medication?
choices: Patient has no interest on learning
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Decreased sensory functions. Decreased sensory functions could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about the newly prescribed medications. Absence of family support and no interest in learning may affect compliance, not knowledge retention. Decreased plasma levels do not alter patient’s knowledge about the drug.

foundation-exam-2.question: When assessing a patient’s level of consciousness, which type of nursing intervention is the nurse performing?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (A) Independent. Independent nursing interventions involve actions that nurses initiate based on their own knowledge and skills without the direction or supervision of another member of the health care team.

foundation-exam-2.question: Claire is admitted with a diagnosis of chronic shoulder pain. By definition, the nurse understands that the patient has had pain for more than:
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) 6 months. Chronic pain is usually defined as pain lasting longer than 6 months.

foundation-exam-2.question: Which of the following statements regarding the nursing process is true?
choices: It is useful on outpatient settings.
It progresses in separate, unrelated steps.
It focuses on the patient, not the nurse.
It provides the solution to all patient health problems.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) It focuses on the patient, not the nurse. The nursing process is patient-centered, not nurse-centered. It can be used in any setting, and the steps are related. The nursing process can’t solve all patient health problems.

foundation-exam-2.question: Which of the following is considered significant enough to require immediate communication to another member of the health care team?
choices: Weight loss of 3 lbs in a 120 lb female patient.
Diminished breath sounds in patient with previously normal breath sounds
Change of heart rate from 70 to 83 beats per minute.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Diminished breath sounds in patient with previously normal breath sounds. Diminished breath sound is a life-threatening problem therefore it is highly priority because they pose the greatest threat to the patient’s well-being.

foundation-exam-2.question: To assess the adequacy of food intake, which of the following assessment parameters is best used?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) 3-day diet recall. 3-day diet recall is an example of dietary history. This is used to indicate the adequacy of food intake of the client.

foundation-exam-2.question: Van Fajardo is a 55 year old who was admitted to the hospital with newly diagnosed hepatitis. The nurse is doing a patient teaching with Mr. Fajardo. What kind of role does the nurse assume?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (B) Teacher. The nurse will assume the role of a teacher in this therapeutic relationship. The other roles are inappropriate in this situation.

foundation-exam-2.question: When providing a continuous enteral feeding, which of the following action is essential for the nurse to do?
choices: Place the client on the left side of the bed.
Attach the feeding bag to the current tubing.
Elevate the head of the bed.
Cold the formula before administering it.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) Elevate the head of the bed. Elevating the head of the bed during an enteral feeding prevents aspiration. The patient may be placed on the right side to prevent aspiration. Enteral feedings are given at room temperature to lessen GI distress. The enteral tubing should be changed every 24 hours to limit microbial growth.

foundation-exam-2.question: Kussmaul’s breathing is;
choices: Prolonged gasping inspiration followed by a very short, usually inefficient expiration.
Marked rhythmic waxing and waning of respirations from very deep to very shallow breathing and temporary apnea.
Increased rate and depth of respiration.
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (D) Increased rate and depth of respiration. Kussmaul breathing is also called hyperventilation. Seen in metabolic acidosis and renal failure. Option A refers to Biot’s breathing. Option B is apneustic breathing and option C is the Cheyne-Stokes breathing.

foundation-exam-2.question: Presty has terminal cancer and she refuses to believe that loss is happening ans she assumes artificial cheerfulness. What stage of grieving is she in?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) Denial. The client is in denial stage because she is unready to face the reality that loss is happening and she assumes artificial cheerfulness.

foundation-exam-2.question: Immunization for healthy babies and preschool children is an example of what level of preventive health care?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (A) Primary. The primary level focuses on health promotion. Secondary level focuses on health maintenance. Tertiary focuses on rehabilitation. There is no curative level of preventive health care problems.

foundation-exam-2.question: Which is an example of a subjective data?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (D) Patient stated, “My arms still hurt.” Subjective data are apparent only to the person affected and can be verified only by that person.

foundation-exam-2.question: The nurse is assessing the endocrine system. Which organ is part of the endocrine system?
foundation-exam-2.explanation: (C) Thyroid. The thyroid is part of the endocrine system. Heart, sinus and thymus are not.

foundation-exam-3.question: Nurse Brenda is teaching a patient about a newly prescribed drug. What could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about prescribed medications?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (B) Sensory deficits. Sensory deficits could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about prescribed medications. Decreased plasma drug levels do not alter the patient’s knowledge about the drug. A lack of family support may affect compliance, not knowledge retention. Toilette syndrome is unrelated to knowledge retention.

foundation-exam-3.question: When examining a patient with abdominal pain the nurse in charge should assess:
choices: The symptomatic quadrant either second or third
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) The symptomatic quadrant last. The nurse should systematically assess all areas of the abdomen, if time and the patient’s condition permit, concluding with the symptomatic area. Otherwise, the nurse may elicit pain in the symptomatic area, causing the muscles in other areas to tighten. This would interfere with further assessment.

foundation-exam-3.question: The nurse is assessing a postoperative adult patient. Which of the following should the nurse document as subjective data?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) Patient’s description of pain. Subjective data come directly from the patient and usually are recorded as direct quotations that reflect the patient’s opinions or feelings about a situation. Vital signs, laboratory test result, and ECG waveforms are examples of objective data.

foundation-exam-3.question: A male patient has a soft wrist-safety device. Which assessment finding should the nurse consider abnormal?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) Cool, pale fingers. A safety device on the wrist may impair circulation and restrict blood supply to body tissues. Therefore, the nurse should assess the patient for signs of impaired circulation, such as cool, pale fingers. A palpable radial or lunar pulse and pink nail beds are normal findings.

foundation-exam-3.question: Which of the following planes divides the body longitudinally into anterior and posterior regions?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (A) Frontal plane. Frontal or coronal plane runs longitudinally at a right angle to a sagittal plane dividing the body in anterior and posterior regions. A sagittal plane runs longitudinally dividing the body into right and left regions; if exactly midline, it is called a midsagittal plane. A transverse plane runs horizontally at a right angle to the vertical axis, dividing the structure into superior and inferior regions.

foundation-exam-3.question: A female patient with a terminal illness is in denial. Indicators of denial include:
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (A) Shock dismay. Shock and dismay are early signs of denial—the first stage of grief. The other options are associated with depression—a later stage of grief.

foundation-exam-3.question: The nurse in charge is transferring a patient from the bed to a chair. Which action does the nurse take during this patient transfer?
choices: Position the head of the bed flat
Helps the patient dangle the legs
Places the chair facing away from the bed
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (B) Helps the patient dangle the legs. After placing the patient in high Fowler’s position and moving the patient to the side of the bed, the nurse helps the patient sit on the edge of the bed and dangle the legs; the nurse then faces the patient and places the chair next to and facing the head of the bed.

foundation-exam-3.question: A female patient who speaks a little English has emergency gallbladder surgery, during discharge preparation, which nursing action would best help this patient understand wound care instruction?
choices: Asking frequently if the patient understands the instruction
Asking an interpreter to replay the instructions to the patient.
Writing out the instructions and having a family member read them to the patient
Demonstrating the procedure and having the patient return the demonstration
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (D) Demonstrating the procedure and having the patient return the demonstration. Demonstrating by the nurse with a return demonstration by the patient ensures that the patient can perform wound care correctly. Patients may claim to understand discharge instruction when they do not. An interpreter of family member may communicate verbal or written instructions inaccurately.

foundation-exam-3.question: Before administering the evening dose of a prescribed medication, the nurse on the evening shift finds an unlabeled, filled syringe in the patient’s medication drawer. What should the nurse in charge do?
choices: Discard the syringe to avoid a medication error
Obtain a label for the syringe from the pharmacy
Use the syringe because it looks like it contains the same medication the nurse was prepared to give
Call the day nurse to verify the contents of the syringe
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (A) Discard the syringe to avoid a medication error. As a safety precaution, the nurse should discard an unlabeled syringe that contains medication. The other options are considered unsafe because they promote error.

foundation-exam-3.question: When administering drug therapy to a male geriatric patient, the nurse must stay especially alert for adverse effects. Which factor makes geriatric patients to adverse drug effects?
choices: Enhanced blood flow to the GI tract
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (B) Aging-related physiological changes. Aging-related physiological changes account for the increased frequency of adverse drug reactions in geriatric patients. Renal and hepatic changes cause drugs to clear more slowly in these patients. With increasing age, neurons are lost and blood flow to the GI tract decreases.

foundation-exam-3.question: A female patient is being discharged after cataract surgery. After providing medication teaching, the nurse asks the patient to repeat the instructions. The nurse is performing which professional role?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (B) Educator. When teaching a patient about medications before discharge, the nurse is acting as an educator. The nurse acts as a manager when performing such activities as scheduling and making patient care assignments. The nurse performs the care giving role when providing direct care, including bathing patients and administering medications and prescribed treatments. The nurse acts as a patient advocate when making the patient’s wishes known to the doctor.

foundation-exam-3.question: A female patient exhibits signs of heightened anxiety. Which response by the nurse is most likely to reduce the patient’s anxiety?
choices: “Read this manual and then ask me any questions you may have.”
“Why don’t you listen to the radio?”
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (D) “Let’s talk about what’s bothering you.” Anxiety may result from feeling of helplessness, isolation, or insecurity. This response helps reduce anxiety by encouraging the patient to express feelings. The nurse should be supportive and develop goals together with the patient to give the patient some control over an anxiety-inducing situation. Because the other options ignore the patient’s feeling and block communication, they would not reduce anxiety.

foundation-exam-3.question: A scrub nurse in the operating room has which responsibility?
choices: Handling surgical instruments to the surgeon
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) Handling surgical instruments to the surgeon. The scrub nurse assist the surgeon by providing appropriate surgical instruments and supplies, maintaining strict surgical asepsis and, with the circulating nurse, accounting for all gauze, sponges, needles, and instruments. The circulating nurse assists the surgeon and scrub nurse, positions the patient, applies appropriate equipment and surgical drapes, assists with gowning and gloving, and provides the surgeon and scrub nurse with supplies.

foundation-exam-3.question: A patient is in the bathroom when the nurse enters to give a prescribed medication. What should the nurse in charge do?
choices: Leave the medication at the patient’s bedside
Tell the patient to be sure to take the medication. And then leave it at the bedside
Return shortly to the patient’s room and remain there until the patient takes the medication
Wait for the patient to return to bed, and then leave the medication at the bedside
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) Return shortly to the patient’s room and remain there until the patient takes the medication. The nurse should return shortly to the patient’s room and remain there until the patient takes the medication to verify that it was taken as directed. The nurse should never leave medication at the patient’s bedside unless specifically requested to do so.

foundation-exam-3.question: The physician orders heparin, 7,500 units, to be administered subcutaneously every 6 hours. The vial reads 10,000 units per millilitre. The nurse should anticipate giving how much heparin for each dose?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) ¾ ml. The nurse solves the problem as follows: 10,000 units/7,500 units = 1 ml/X. 10,000X = 7,500. X = 7,500/10,000 or ¾ ml.

foundation-exam-3.question: The nurse in charge measures a patient’s temperature at 102 degrees F. what is the equivalent Centigrade temperature?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) 38.9 degrees C. To convert Fahrenheit degrees to centigrade, use this formula: C degrees = (F degrees – 32) × 5/9. C degrees = (102 – 32) × 5/9 = 38.9 degrees C.

foundation-exam-3.question: To evaluate a patient for hypoxia, the physician is most likely to order which laboratory test?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (D) Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis. All of these tests help evaluate a patient with respiratory problems. However, ABG analysis is the only test that evaluates gas exchange in the lungs, providing information about the patient’s oxygenation status.

foundation-exam-3.question: The nurse uses a stethoscope to auscultate a male patient’s chest. Which statement about a stethoscope with a bell and diaphragm is true?
choices: The bell detects high-pitched sounds best
The diaphragm detects high-pitched sounds best
The diaphragm detects low-pitched sounds best
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (B) The diaphragm detects high-pitched sounds best. The diaphragm of a stethoscope detects high-pitched sounds best; the bell detects low-pitched sounds best. Palpation detects thrills best.

foundation-exam-3.question: A male patient is to be discharged with a prescription for an analgesic that is a controlled substance. During discharge teaching, the nurse should explain that the patient must fill this prescription how soon after the date on which it was written?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) Within 6 months. In most cases, an outpatient must fill a prescription for a controlled substance within 6 months of the date on which the prescription was written.

foundation-exam-3.question: Which human element considered by the nurse in charge during assessment can affect drug administration?
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (D) The patient’s cognitive abilities. The nurse must consider the patient’s cognitive abilities to understand drug instructions. If not, the nurse must find a family member or significant other to take on the responsibility of administering medications in the home setting. The patient’s ability to recover, occupational hazards, and socioeconomic status do not affect drug administration.

foundation-exam-3.question: When explaining the initiation of I.V. therapy to a 2-year-old child, the nurse should:
choices: Ask the child, “Do you want me to start the I.V. now?”
Give simple directions shortly before the I.V. therapy is to start
Tell the child, “This treatment is for your own good”
Inform the child that the needle will be in place for 10 days
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (B) Give simple directions shortly before the I.V. therapy is to start. Because a 2-year-old child has limited understanding, the nurse should give simple directions and explanations of what will occur shortly before the procedure. She should try to avoid frightening the child with the explanation and allow the child to make simple choices, such as choosing the I.V. insertion site, if possible. However, she shouldn’t ask the child if he wants the therapy, because the answer may be “No!” Telling the child that the treatment is for his own good is ineffective because a 2-year-old perceives pain as a negative sensation and cannot understand that a painful procedure can have positive results. Telling the child how long the therapy will last is ineffective because the 2-year-old doesn’t have a good understanding of time.

foundation-exam-3.question: All of the following parts of the syringe are sterile except the:
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (A) Barrel. All syringes have three parts: a tip, which connects the needle to the syringe; a barrel, the outer part on which the measurement scales are printed; and a plunger, which fits inside the barrel to expel the medication. The external part of the barrel and the plunger (flange) must be handled during the preparation and administration of the injection. However, the inside and tip of the barrel, the inside (shaft) of the plunger, and the needle tip must remain sterile until after the injection.

foundation-exam-3.question: The best way to instill eye drops is to:
choices: Instruct the patient to look upward, and drop the medication into the center of the lower lid
Instruct the patient to look ahead, and drop the medication into the center of the lower lid
Drop the medication into the inner canthus regardless of eye position
Drop the medication into the center of the canthus regardless of eye position
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (A) Instruct the patient to look upward, and drop the medication into the center of the lower lid. Having the patient look upward reduces blinking and protects the cornea. Instilling drops in the center of the lower lid promotes absorption because the drops are less likely to run into the nasolacrimal duct or out of the eye.

foundation-exam-3.question: The difference between an 18G needle and a 25G needle is the needle’s:
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (C) Thickness. Gauge is a measure of the needle’s thickness: The higher the number, the thinner the shaft. Therefore, an 18G needle is considerably thicker than a 25G needle.

foundation-exam-3.question: A patient receiving an anticoagulant should be assessed for signs of:
foundation-exam-3.explanation: (A) Hypotension. A major side effect of anticoagulant therapy is bleeding, which can be identified by hypotension (a systolic blood pressure under 100 mm Hg). Anticoagulants do not result in the other three conditions.

pnle-exam-1.question: A 10 year old who has sustained a head injury is brought to the emergency department by his mother. A diagnosis of a mild concussion is made. At the time of discharge, nurse Ron should instruct the mother to:
choices: Withhold food and fluids for 24 hours.
Allow him to play outdoors with his friends.
Arrange for a follow up visit with the child’s primary care provider in one week.
Check for any change in responsiveness every two hours until the follow-up visit.
pnle-exam-1.explanation: Check for any change in responsiveness every two hours until the follow-up visit. Assessing neurological status and responsiveness closely is critical following a head injury to catch signs of worsening intracranial pressure or delayed complications early.

pnle-exam-1.question: A male client has suffered a motor accident and is now suffering from hypovolemic shock. Nurse Helen should frequency assess the client’s vital signs during the compensatory stage of shock, because:
choices: Decreased contractility of the heart occurs
The parasympathetic nervous system is triggered
pnle-exam-1.explanation: Arteriolar constriction occurs. During the compensatory stage of shock, the sympathetic nervous system triggers peripheral vasoconstriction (arteriolar constriction) to maintain blood pressure and perfusion to vital organs.

pnle-exam-1.question: A paranoid male client with schizophrenia is losing weight, reluctant to eat, and voicing concerns about being poisoned. The best intervention by nurse Dina would be to:
choices: Allow the client to open canned or pre-packaged food
Restrict the client to his room until 2 lbs are gained
Have a staff member personally taste all of the client’s food
Tell the client the food has been x-rayed by the staff and is safe
pnle-exam-1.explanation: Allow the client to open canned or pre-packaged food. Allowing a paranoid patient to open sealed, pre-packaged, or canned food provides them a sense of security and control, which reduces fear of poisoning and encourages nutritional intake.

pnle-exam-1.question: One day the mother of a young adult confides to nurse Frida that she is very troubled by he child’s emotional illness. The nurse’s most therapeutic initial response would be:
choices: “You may be able to lessen your feelings of guilt by seeking counseling”
“It would be helpful if you become involved in volunteer work at this time”
“I recognize it’s hard to deal with this, but try to remember that this too shall pass”
“Joining a support group of parents who are coping with this problem can be quite helpful.”
pnle-exam-1.explanation: “Joining a support group of parents who are coping with this problem can be quite helpful.” Connecting with peer support groups provides validation, reduces isolation, and offers practical coping strategies from others in similar situations.

pnle-exam-1.question: To check for wound hemorrhage after a client has had a surgery for the removal of a tumor in the neck, nurse grace should:
